newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Pele wants to privatize Brazil's soccer clubs.
newsitem.headline: Pele wants to privatize Brazil's soccer clubs.

text.p: Pele, Brazil's soccer hero and special sports minister, has proposed that Brazilian soccer clubs be turned into private enterprises to make them more accountable.

Pele, whose name is Edson Arantes do Nascimento, plans to submit to Congress next month a bill to clear the way for soccer clubs, which have thousands of members and function as all-around sports clubs, to become private firms, his spokesman confirmed on Friday.
"What people want to do, in truth, is to clean up football; and that's in everyone's interest," Pele was quoted as saying by Brazilian papers.
"Currently, clubs don't give an accounting to anyone, because they are non-profit entities," he said.
The new legislation, which is expected to face stiff opposition from the clubs, would give teams until 1999 to become private enterprises.

It is not the first time Pele has butted heads with the clubs. He recently upset club managements by pushing through a law, which takes effect next year, enabling players to be free agents after a certain age.
